header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, CIRCUIT COURT, LARKANA
Crl. Misc. Application No. S- 11 of 2026
through Mr. Athar Abbas Solangi, Advocate.
State : Through Mr. Aitbar Ali Bullo, DPG.
through Mr. Safdar Ali Ghouri, Advocate.
body: Arbab Ali Hakro, J.- Through this application under section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (“Cr.P.C.”), the applicant has called in question the legality and propriety of the order dated 02.01.2026 (“the impugned order”) passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge/ Ex-Officio Justice of Peace-IV, Larkana (“the Justice of Peace”) in Crl. Misc. Application No.2089 of 2025. By that order his application under section 22-A(6)(i), Cr.P.C., seeking a direction to the SHO, Police Station Civil Line, Larkana to record his statement under section 154, Cr.P.C. against respondent No.3, was dismissed.

2. Briefly, the applicant’s version is that respondent No.3 purchased his land situated in Deh and Tapo Dodai, Taluka and District Larkana, and, in respect of the sale consideration, issued a cheque for Rs.3,65,00,000/-, which was returned unpaid on presentation. When the amount was demanded, he was first put off and then threatened. The learned Justice of Peace, relying on the police reports, treated the dispute as civil in nature and declined the direction.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant, while drawing attention to paragraph 6 of the impugned order, submits that the applicant was not heard at all and that the application was decided after hearing only the learned DDPP and the counsel for the proposed accused. He further submits that a request for time was made on behalf of the applicant, which was declined, and that the impugned order was thus passed without affording him an opportunity of hearing.

4. When confronted with this position, learned counsel for respondent No.3 and the learned DPG, though they maintain that the respondent has a good case on the merits, do not oppose the matter being sent back for decision afresh after hearing the applicant. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 has filed a statement, along with copies of the agreement, counterfoils of six cheques, and other documents, which are taken on record; copies thereof have been supplied to the learned DPG and learned counsel for the applicant.

5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and the learned DPG, and have gone through the record. The impugned order itself bears out the grievance. Paragraph 4 records that the applicant and his counsel were called absent; paragraph 6 shows that only the learned DDPP and the counsel for the proposed accused were heard; and paragraph 8 notes that, on the second call, a junior counsel was in attendance, yet the matter was proceeded with, and the papers filed by the applicant were treated as his arguments. The learned Justice of Peace did not stop at that. He went on to record findings on the merits adverse to the applicant, namely that he had concealed an earlier payment, that the agreement appeared to have been tampered with, and that he had not come with clean hands. Findings of this kind ought not to be returned against a party who has not been heard on them. The functions of an Ex-Officio Justice of Peace under section 22-A(6), Cr.P.C., are quasijudicial. He is to examine the record, hear the parties, and then pass an order with due application of mind, as held by the Supreme Court in Younas Abbas . With junior counsel present in Court, the matter could well have been kept aside or put off to a short date. To that extent, the impugned order falls short of the requirement of a fair hearing and cannot be sustained, especially when neither the respondent nor the State opposes a fresh decision.

6. Accordingly, and with the consent of the parties, the impugned order dated 02.01.2026 is set aside. Crl. Misc. Application No.2089 of 2025 shall be deemed pending before the learned Additional Sessions Judge/Ex-Officio Justice of Peace-IV, Larkana, who shall decide it afresh by a speaking order, in accordance with law, after providing both parties with an equal opportunity of Younas Abbas and others v. Additional Sessions Judge, Chakwal and others PLD 2016 SC 581 hearing and considering the material placed before him, within twenty-five (25) days from the date of receipt of this order. The parties shall be at liberty to place their respective documents before him. Nothing in this order shall be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case, which shall be decided by the learned Justice of Peace independently.
7. The instant criminal miscellaneous application stands disposed of in the above terms. Office shall send a copy of this order to the learned Justice of Peace for compliance.
